Perfect correlation is a statistical artifact of multiple-comparison hunting across 36 tested lags and 6 instrument pairs (216 total comparisons), and the 1.000 agreement is noise masquerading as signal because the chance threshold for the best match across all offsets tried is ±0.287—a threshold that scales with repeated testing.

A transient environmental or operational disturbance on Day 20 (temperature spike, vibration, power event, or operator procedure break) synchronized elevated scatter across all four channels without producing a persistent drift or level shift; Day 30 scatter is a separate, independent realization of the same underlying noise distribution and does NOT indicate that Day 20 is repeating.

Day 20 operator, calibration, or procedural anomaly (skipped calibration check, operator fatigue, instrument handling incident, brief power transient, or logging misconfiguration) that increased measurement noise locally without leaving impossible or out-of-envelope values; Day 30 scatter is independent and unrelated to Day 20.

Day 20 and Day 30 scatter are both independent samples from the same underlying white or near-white noise distribution with SD ~0.02–0.03 per channel; no systematic cause is required, and the similarity in scatter magnitude is pure coincidence.

Data integrity issue in my own cross-check computation: the 1.000 pendulum_lab ↔ resonator_obs agreement at 3-day lag is a reporting error, duplicate paste, or unintended data merge, and must be re-examined by re-running the correlation from raw logs.

pendulum_obs has drifted or shifted its calibration between baseline and post-baseline periods; the Day 33 level change is the visible edge of an actual instrumental drift that began earlier but only became statistically clear by Day 33 due to sample accumulation.

A transient external disturbance (thermal, vibrational, electromagnetic, or operational) affected the pendulum_obs measurement chain specifically on Days 32–33, raising noise or inducing a temporary systematic offset that does not reflect true pendulum period change and will not persist if the disturbance is isolated.

The perfect 1.000 correlation between pendulum_lab and resonator_obs at 3-day lag (n=102) is a data integrity error—duplicate data pasted into both columns, a trial-indexing misalignment, or a computation mistake in my cross-check script—and does not reflect a real physical signal. Removal of this erroneous correlation restores confidence in independent measurement channels.

Day 20 and Day 33 represent independent realizations of elevated noise in the measurement system(s), both driven by random process variation or separate transient environmental events, with no systematic cause or cross-day connection. The statistical synchronization of Day 20 scatter across all four channels was coincidental or driven by an unrecorded one-time event; Day 33 anomaly in pendulum_obs alone reflects a separate, unrelated disturbance.

The Day 33 level change in pendulum_obs is a statistical artifact of small-sample variance at the tail of the dataset (trials 193–198 represent only 6 final trials out of 198 total); the z≈3.2 flag is a false positive from multiple-comparison corrections or a binning artifact, and no real anomaly exists.
Day 34 pendulum_lab cluster is the leading edge of instrumental drift that will persist into subsequent days
Day 34 pendulum_lab cluster and Day 33 pendulum_obs level change are independent transient disturbances (separate events affecting each channel), not systematic drift

Perfect 1.000 correlation between pendulum_lab and resonator_obs (3-day lag, n=102) is a data integrity error (duplicate, misalignment, or computation bug), invalidating any cross-channel inference until resolved

The Day 33 pendulum_obs level change (z≈3.2) is a statistical artifact from post-hoc boundary scanning or inadequate multiplicity correction; the flagged anomaly is a false positive and should be disregarded pending clarification of the statistical test
Perfect correlation is a data handling error: trial-log misalignment, accidental duplication, or computation bug in cross-check code
Perfect correlation is genuine but reflects an unsuspected coupling mechanism (shared thermal mass, mechanical resonance, or electromagnetic coupling between pendulum_lab and resonator_obs apparatus)
